# EvKbd

> A Kbd (keyboard key) is a small inline chip that represents a single physical key or shortcut token — like Ctrl or ⇧ — used to document keyboard shortcuts.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:kbd` |
| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |
| Import | `import { EvKbd } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvKbd>` or `<ev-kbd>` |
| Source | `src/atoms/kbd/EvKbd.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<kbd class="ev-kbd">` |

</EvKbd>

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Kbd**, frame `4527:86976` (Kbd). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use to render keyboard keys and shortcuts inline — in menus, tooltips, help text, or command palettes (e.g. Ctrl + K). Combine several Kbd chips for a key combo.

### When not to use

- Don't use as an interactive button — it's a display token, not a control. Don't use it for general inline code or labels; use a code style or badge (`evoq-ui:badge`) instead.

### Do

- Use the Icon variant for modifier keys (⇧ ⌘ ⌥) and Text for named keys. Pick Light=No on dark surfaces so the chip stays legible. Match the platform's key conventions.

### Don't

- Don't cram long words into a single key chip — keep each Kbd to one key or short token. Don't mix Light=Yes and Light=No chips in the same shortcut.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvKbd`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<kbd class="ev-kbd">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:kbd` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
